claim_summary: Moirai Agent documents two composable forecasting procedures: context-aware forecast adaptation and LLM-based selection of a forecasting expert.

claim_evidence.quote: This repository provides an early research preview and enables replication of benchmark results for two independent yet composable agents.

First, it enables context-aware forecasting by combining numerical history with external contextual inputs to refine lookback windows, detect anomalies, and anticipate future effects. Second, it performs expert selection through an LLM-based selector that chooses the most suitable forecasting model for each task from a pool of state-of-the-art forecasters.

modules.name: Context-aware forecast adaptation
modules.scope_reason: The procedure is explicitly for context-aware forecasting and refines forecast lookback windows. Under R3_1, its core logic serves the forecasting output requirement; if the task family changed, the forecast-refinement objective would need redesign. The temporal-window operation alone does not make it GTS, and it is not task-independent GH.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - explicitly a forecasting procedure that refines forecast lookback windows

evidence.quote: First, it enables context-aware forecasting by combining numerical history with external contextual inputs to refine lookback windows, detect anomalies, and anticipate future effects.

modules.name: Forecasting expert selection
modules.scope_reason: The selector chooses a forecasting model for each task. Under R3_1, its selection objective is tied to the forecasting task family; changing the task family would require changing the expert-selection objective and pool. It is not a task-independent temporal service (GTS) or general runtime mechanism (GH).
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - selects a forecaster for the forecasting task

reconciliation.reason: The README describes two independent yet composable agents: one refines forecasts using numerical history and external context, while the other selects a forecaster. These are separately described mechanisms, so the existing combined module is split; the existing ID is retained for context-aware forecast adaptation and a new ID is assigned to expert selection. The packet supports forecasting-task scope but does not establish infrastructure as the contribution.

notes: The packet is an official repository README rather than a paper text. It identifies two composable agents but provides no experiment details or measured results.
